title.narrative: Integrated Food Production Response Project to the Famine Affected Community in Mukjar, Wasat Jabal Marrah and Shamal Jabal Marrah localities in Central Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtAccording to the latest Sudan IPC Famine Review Committee (FRC), famine conditions are projected between December 2024 and May 2025 in several states, with only minor improvements in acute food insecurity compared to the lean season. Currently, 24.6 million people face high levels of acute food insecurity, including 1,074,329 individuals categorized as IPC 3+ in Central Darfur. The ongoing conflict has triggered a severe and widening food and nutrition crisis, causing mass displacement, particularly from North Darfur to the Jebel Marrah area. This is compounded by an ailing economy, the collapse of essential social services, societal disruptions, and persistent gender disparities. Since the war began, Central Darfur has hosted approximately 923,814 displaced individuals from North Darfur, South Darfur, Khartoum, and other states.ltbrgtProject ObjectivesltbrgtThe project aims to provide integrated food production, general protection, WASH, and emergency shelter/non-food items (ES/NFI) to newly displaced people, returnees, and nomadic communities at risk of famine in Mukjar, Central, and North Jebel Marrah localities of Central Darfur. It will benefit 296,148 individuals (106,178 women, 91,375 girls, 53,500 men, and 45,095 boys), including 152,581 IDPs, 33,131 returnees, and 110,436 host community members, including nomadic and pastoral populations.ltbrgtEmergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ES/NFI)ltbrgtThe project will provide emergency shelter materials (plastic sheets, poles, ropes, pegs) and essential non-food items (warm clothing such as jackets and coats) to 10,000 crisis-affected households living in temporary shelters or gathering points. This will ensure protection, safety, security, and dignity for vulnerable populations.ltbrgtFood Security and Livelihoods (FSL)ltbrgtThe project will promote food production through the distribution of agricultural seeds, tools, and animal vaccinations. Additionally, it will provide agricultural extension services to improve productivity, fostering household self-reliance and resilience in food security.ltbrgtGeneral ProtectionltbrgtThis component will address protection needs by enhancing preparedness, mitigating risks, and implementing protection monitoring. Activities include crop protection measures, early warning capacity building, and efforts to address the root causes of violations, particularly regarding access to natural resources.ltbrgtWASHltbrgtThe project will improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks. Activities include rehabilitating water points, constructing latrines, and conducting hygiene promotion campaigns. Community-led total sanitation (CLTS) approaches will ensure sustainability and community ownership.ltbrgtImplementation StrategyltbrgtThe project employs a consortium approach with WR as the lead organization, partnering with VSFG, JMCO, and HOPE, each bringing extensive experience and strong community relationships. This coordinated, area-based approach ensures comprehensive sectoral coverage, effective service delivery, conflict sensitivity, and equitable resource distribution. Community engagement, consultation with local authorities, and alignment with relevant clusters will support successful implementation.ltbrgtConflict Sensitivity and Social CohesionltbrgtThe project prioritizes conflict-sensitive programming to reduce tensions, biases, or inequities in resource allocation. Efforts will focus on fostering social cohesion among community leaders and authorities while addressing the complex conflict dynamics in Central Darfur.ltbrgtCross-Cutting ThemesltbrgtCross-cutting themes, including protection mainstreaming, gender equality, disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations (AAP), will be integrated across all activities. This ensures a safe, inclusive, responsive, and rights-based approach.lt/pgt
